objective: Publish actionable failure evidence idempotently without losing it on dedupe or partial API failure.
acceptanceCriteria:
Repeated identical evidence produces one issue and no duplicate comment; lookup failure produces no issue.
Dedupe against an existing issue never discards current evidence, and a transport retry cannot blindly create a duplicate.
All published references are repository-qualified; #1 history remains preserved.
Collector and publication receipts expose partial/limited results; issue count never exceeds one new canonical issue per run.
nonGoals: No cross-repository issue pair, intake defect resolution, lifecycle implementation routing or recovery-run dispatch.
risks: risk:medium: Adopt one canonical issue in the configured Factory repository per project+normalized signature fingerprint. This supersedes the parent's unresolved one-versus-two issue choice: no second project issue is created by the audit. Build evidence before GitHub access and dedupe by an exact HTML marker containing a stable fingerprint that excludes volatile run IDs/timestamps. Project/known issue references use fully qualified URLs. Any lookup/auth/API failure aborts publication; it is never treated as an empty search. Existing exact marker means append/update bounded evidence only when new, with a receipt recording existing/created/failed. Adopt existing legacy issues only with unambiguous repository/project/signature evidence; preserve human body/comments, and flag ambiguous matches for review. Link existing #1 and its historical evidence without claiming intake fixed. Persist publication receipt before retry; after ambiguous create failure, requery marker before another write. No inferred close/resolve or restart.
suggestedWorkBreakdown:
Implement artifact-consuming publisher and exact marker matching, including checked gh exit codes.
Use one canonical Factory issue, render redacted source evidence and qualified existing-project links consistently.
Wire collector/publisher as separate workflow command steps and align the skill's read/write/issue-count contract.
Test retries, ambiguous transport outcome, lookup failure, same-repository target, legacy adoption and repeated evidence.
